tools.does: Line up residues to establish positional homology
tools.analogue: Align sentences or plot beats of two works by their unit vectors (dynamic programming, unit-profile similarity as the score)
tools.experiment: Align the 9 adaptation/source pairs; score against human-marked matching scenes. Rival: sentence-embedding DTW; word overlap per sentence

tools.does: Search a database for homologues with an E-value
tools.analogue: Query a story's profile against a profile database; E-value from a background of ordinary works (the 69-film bar is the seed)
tools.feasibility: Yes, on a new corpus. Low novelty
tools.experiment: Name-free retrieval of documented remakes and sources. Rival: BM25, e5 embeddings. Study: TF-IDF already finds sources as well (`experiments.json`)

tools.does: Infer trees with a model and support values
tools.analogue: Likelihood/Bayesian tree on binary unit characters (Mk or Dollo), bootstrap over units
tools.experiment: Bootstrap the Batman tree; test recovery of documented-relative triplets. Rival: same on word presence. Note the study's tree is star-like ("most internal branches are much shorter than the branch to each work", paper Fig. 4 caption)

tools.does: Tree from shared gene presence
tools.analogue: Exactly what the study did (Jaccard + neighbour-joining)
tools.experiment: Compare to a Dollo model that forbids regaining a lost meme. Rival: word presence

tools.does: Show conflict and reticulation instead of forcing a tree
tools.analogue: Network of works; delta score for tree-likeness
tools.experiment: Is Batman less tree-like than the cousins? Rival: network from TF-IDF distances. Precedent: Cinderella (Sakamoto Martini, Kendal and Tehrani 2023)

tools.does: Convert divergence to time
tools.analogue: Rate of meme turnover per year; date an undated work
tools.feasibility: Speculative. On this corpus (32 tips, gap 1967 to 1985, modern summaries)
tools.experiment: Root-to-tip regression of meme distance on year over 500+ franchise works. Rival: lexical distance on year. Precedent: Gray and Atkinson 2003; Pagel et al. 2007

tools.does: Infer and resurrect ancestral states
tools.analogue: Infer the meme set of an unrecorded ancestor; have an LLM write it; read it back
tools.feasibility: Yes, from data already committed. For inference
tools.experiment: Hide one known intermediate (e.g. Year One), predict its meme set from neighbours. Rival: predict its word set from neighbours; an LLM guessing from reading neighbours. Precedent: da Silva and Tehrani 2016

tools.does: Ratio of protein-changing to silent change; purifying vs positive selection
tools.analogue: Ratio of concept-unit change to wording change, normalised by the same ratio under paraphrase
tools.feasibility: Blocked until units are shown to survive rewording
tools.experiment: See seed 6 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: embedding distance over lexical distance

tools.does: Fixed vs polymorphic, by class of site
tools.analogue: 2x2: {concept, word-like units} x {fixed between two franchises, variable within}
tools.needs: Two franchises, 20+ works each; unit classes
tools.feasibility: Blocked until units are shown to survive rewording and a new corpus
tools.experiment: Batman vs Superman lineages. Rival: LLM-coded tropes vs word types in the same 2x2

tools.tool: Selective sweeps, hitch-hiking (Maynard Smith and Haigh 1974; Sabeti 2002)
tools.does: Find recent selection from linked diversity loss
tools.analogue: A hit work drags a bundle of memes to high frequency, passengers included
tools.experiment: Do Nolan-era optional memes sweep through non-Batman superhero films after 2008? Rival: phrase-frequency series; embedding-cluster frequency. Precedent: Ackland et al. 2007; Yeh, Fogarty and Kandler 2019

tools.does: Detect departures from neutral equilibrium in the frequency spectrum
tools.analogue: Frequency spectrum of memes across contemporaneous works
tools.feasibility: Yes, from data already committed. But validity low (3% threshold noise makes fake singletons)
tools.experiment: Compare the unit spectrum to one generated by threshold noise alone. Rival: word-type spectrum

tools.tool: Fst and population structure (Lewontin and Krakauer 1973; Pritchard et al. 2000)
tools.does: Differentiation between populations; outlier loci; admixture fractions
tools.analogue: Per-meme Fst between franchises, media, eras; admixture fractions per work
tools.experiment: ADMIXTURE-style clustering of the 114 works, name-free. Rival: an LDA topic model on words (the same model family as STRUCTURE; confirmed by the checker: Wikipedia's "Latent Dirichlet allocation" page says the model was first presented for population genetics by Pritchard, Stephens and Donnelly in 2000, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latent_Dirichlet_allocation). Precedent: Ross, Greenhill and Atkinson 2013

tools.does: Genealogy backward in time; effective population size
tools.analogue: Effective number of parent works behind a later work
tools.experiment: Estimate how many sources explain an adaptation's optional memes. Rival: same with words

tools.does: Non-random association of alleles
tools.analogue: Memes that travel together (secret identity + origin in loss + costume)
tools.experiment: Do LD blocks in the ordinary-film pool match known genre templates? Rival: word co-occurrence (PMI) blocks

tools.tool: Epistasis, fitness landscapes (Sarkisyan 2016; Wright 1932 `[UNVERIFIED exact citation; no DOI found]`)
tools.does: Effect of a mutation depends on background
tools.analogue: Meme A helps only with meme B
tools.feasibility: Yes, on a new corpus. Via generated stories
tools.experiment: 2^5 factorial of planted memes, rated by readers. Rival: the planted design matrix itself (neurons add nothing here except as a readout check)

tools.does: All single mutants x a fitness assay
tools.analogue: All single edits of a text x clicks, ratings or recall
tools.feasibility: Yes, on a new corpus. Data exists (Upworthy archive, 32,487 experiments; Matias et al. 2021)
tools.experiment: See seed 3 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: words (Robertson et al. 2023), embeddings, an LLM reading the headline

tools.does: Iterate mutate and select
tools.analogue: Evolve texts under a rater; watch which units fix
tools.experiment: 20 replicate lines; do the same units fix in parallel? Rival: parallelism in words and in LLM-coded tropes. Precedents: Promptbreeder, FunSearch, AlphaEvolve

tools.does: Replay evolution in replicate lines
tools.analogue: Long LLM or human transmission chains
tools.experiment: Do core units survive 50 retellings more than optional ones? Rival: content-word survival. Precedent: Perez et al. 2024 (attractors)

tools.does: Knock out each gene, read the phenotype
tools.analogue: Ablate or steer each unit in the writer model, read the text and its reception
tools.feasibility: Yes, on a new corpus. The one tool with no word-level twin inside the generator
tools.experiment: See seed 4 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: prompt instruction "omit X"; keyword logit ban; random-unit ablation

tools.does: Genome-wide association with a trait, corrected for structure
tools.analogue: Unit-wide association with box office, ratings, virality, with genre/era/length as covariates
tools.experiment: See seed 8 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: word-level association; embedding ridge; LLM-rated features. Warning: length alone gives AUC 0.756 against hero films (`experiments.json`, `length_only_auc_vs_hero`)

tools.does: Map trait loci in controlled crosses
tools.analogue: Cross two parent stories; map which parental memes drive offspring ratings
tools.experiment: See seed 9 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: planted labels + an LLM reader

tools.does: Detect gene flow between non-sister lineages
tools.analogue: Borrowing across franchises (crossovers, homage)
tools.experiment: See seed 5 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: the same D statistic on word presence. Context: Greenhill et al. 2009; Collard et al. 2006

tools.does: Find breakpoints where ancestry switches
tools.analogue: Paint each sentence of a work by the source it descends from
tools.experiment: Paint The Dark Knight by Long Halloween vs Killing Joke (both listed as sources in `experiments.json` E2 rows). Rival: nearest-source by sentence embedding; word overlap

tools.does: Core vs accessory; open vs closed
tools.analogue: The canon tiers (56 / 194 / 14,593; `canon.json`)
tools.experiment: See seed 7 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: word-type accumulation (Heaps' law)

tools.does: Conserved gene order
tools.analogue: Conserved order of memes through a plot (Propp claimed a fixed order of functions)
tools.experiment: Is core-meme order more conserved in Batman than under sentence shuffling? Rival: sentiment-arc and embedding trajectories (Reagan et al. 2016)

tools.does: Group homologous domains
tools.analogue: Within a model: the 14,843 families. Across models: twins, crosscoders, universal SAEs
tools.feasibility: Done within; a new corpus across
tools.experiment: Families with members in all of 5 models, on name-free text. Rival: nearest single word (the study's word-matched null)

tools.does: Controlled vocabulary with evidence codes
tools.analogue: Unit labels with evidence codes: read from examples; passed blind test; confirmed by steering
tools.feasibility: Yes: partly from committed data, partly on a new corpus
tools.experiment: Map 200 families to TV Tropes entries; test on held-out tagged works. Rival: zero-shot LLM trope tagging. Assets: Transluce descriptions for every Llama 3.1 8B Instruct MLP neuron (458,752 neurons; Choi et al., 23 October 2024, https://transluce.org/neuron-descriptions; the same model variant the study used, `study/paper/paper.md` section 2.2); `study/results/robustness/label_test.json`

tools.does: Profile an environment without culturing
tools.analogue: Profile a whole feed or forum without segmenting into works
tools.experiment: Detect the arrival of a documented narrative earlier than a keyword tracker. Rival: keyword and phrase clustering (Leskovec et al. 2009); embedding clusters

tools.does: Short standard marker identifies species
tools.analogue: A small unit set identifies a franchise
tools.experiment: Study: name-free AUC 0.52 (Qwen) and 0.54 (Llama) vs masked-hero films; a TF-IDF centroid gets 0.80 (`experiments.json`). Next: supervised barcode over 10 franchises. Rival: supervised words

tools.does: Map lineages onto geography
tools.analogue: Map variants onto languages, countries, platforms
tools.experiment: Same film's plot in 10 language Wikipedias: do profiles cluster by film or by language? Rival: multilingual-e5; translate then TF-IDF. Precedent: Bortolini et al. 2017

tools.does: Real-time trees with growth rates per clade
tools.analogue: Live tree of narrative variants; forecast which clade grows
tools.experiment: Predict next month's growing clades (Łuksza and Lässig 2014; Neher et al. 2014). Rival: count extrapolation; edit-distance trees (Adamic et al. 2016)

tools.does: Mutant cloud around a master sequence; error threshold
tools.analogue: A meme as a variant cloud; a copy-fidelity threshold below which identity dissolves
tools.experiment: Chains at 5 fidelity levels x 20 replicates; where do core units collapse? Rival: content-word survival; LLM judge of gist

tools.does: Drift as the null
tools.analogue: Random copying as the null for meme frequency change
tools.feasibility: Yes: partly from committed data, partly on a new corpus
tools.experiment: See seed 2 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: word types under the same test. Precedents: Bentley et al. 2004; Kandler and Shennan 2013

tools.does: Reject drift from frequency trajectories
tools.analogue: Frequency-increment test per unit across decades
tools.experiment: As S2. Caveat: binning artefacts (Karjus et al. 2020). Precedent: Newberry et al. 2017

tools.does: Split change into selection and transmission
tools.analogue: Selection among parent works vs transformation during adaptation, per unit
tools.feasibility: Yes, on a new corpus (Wikidata "based on")
tools.experiment: Is the transformation term larger than the selection term? That is Sperber vs Dawkins in one number. Rival: same split with LLM-coded tropes. Theory: El Mouden et al. 2014

tools.does: Parent/offspring regression; response to selection
tools.analogue: Per-unit heritability across source/adaptation pairs
tools.experiment: Is heritability of concept-labelled units above that of word-like units, name-free? Rival: per-word heritability; per-embedding-dimension heritability

tools.does: One molecule shared by all life gives one tree
tools.analogue: A unit set with twins in every model (the P2 claim, narrowed)
tools.experiment: See seed 10 in notes/l7-biology-toolkit.md. Rival: random unit sets; word presence

tools.does: Give every base call its own error estimate
tools.analogue: Grade each presence call by how strongly the unit fired: its band in its own range, or its rank among the token's strongest units
tools.experiment: In Goodfire's companion paper a description picks the firing passage 86% of the time in the weakest band studied and 95% in the strongest. Test whether stronger calls recur more often across two summaries of one story. Rival: the study's film-relative rule

tools.does: Tell a gene shared by descent between species from a copy inside one genome
tools.analogue: Matched neurons in two models are orthologs; neurons copied between layers of one model are paralogs
tools.experiment: Census of same-index copies in Qwen3-8B, then recount meme families and twins without them. Control: different-index pairs at the same layer gap

tools.does: Locate genes from start, stop and splice signals
tools.analogue: Units that fire on a full stop, a comma or 'but' at a story turn mark where a beat ends, not what it contains
tools.experiment: Place annotated turning points with punctuation stripped. Rival: position alone; an LLM asked to mark the turns. Boundary units should be kept out of trees

landmarks.gave: A naming and ranking system, with no mechanism.
landmarks.memetic: Already exists: folktale type and motif indexes, TV Tropes. Neurons give an automatic version, with labels only partly checked.
landmarks.statusText: exists by hand; automatic version unvalidated

landmarks.memetic: Already exists by analogy: Dawkins, Cavalli-Sforza and Feldman, Boyd and Richerson. The idea is not what is missing.

landmarks.gave: Inheritance in discrete particles, shown by ratios in controlled crosses of seven clean traits.
landmarks.memetic: The right next target. A few clean units, planted in stories and crossed under control. Mendel picked 7 traits, not 14,843.
landmarks.statusText: not attempted; planted stories are the true-breeding lines

landmarks.gave: An ordering whose gaps predicted elements nobody had found.
landmarks.memetic: A table of memes whose gaps predict workable combinations nobody has used. Needs a low-dimensional structure in unit space. Nobody has shown one.

landmarks.gave: Mendel and Darwin joined by population genetics.
landmarks.memetic: The mathematics was written without a unit. Units would supply its parameters: copying fidelity and selection strength. Comes after the Mendel and Kimura steps.

landmarks.gave: One gene, one enzyme: a clean rule that later needed a finer unit (split genes, alternative splicing).
landmarks.memetic: The essay's one neuron, one job, and the companion paper's revision a month later: 47% of neuron poles have one role, 69% one dominant role, and the rest are told apart by context. A pole is the wrong character for a tree wherever it has two roles.

landmarks.gave: Which substance carries heredity: strip components and see what still transmits.
landmarks.memetic: Name removal was step one: heredity survived without names. Step two, strip the wording by paraphrase or translation, is not done and is cheap.

landmarks.gave: The supernormal stimulus: a dummy that triggers an instinct harder than the real thing.
landmarks.memetic: Goodfire's agents wrote text that fired 120 of 128 neuron poles harder than anything in a 10-billion-token corpus. If the unit keys on an idea, readers will rate that text a stronger example. If it keys on a token, they will not.
landmarks.statusText: shown for neurons, untested for ideas

landmarks.gave: A physical structure that explains copying.
landmarks.memetic: Not available for human culture: a model neuron is an instrument, not the substrate in a human head. Possible for ideas passed between models, where weights can be read.
landmarks.statusText: out of reach for human minds

landmarks.gave: The first cheap measure of variation, applied widely.
landmarks.memetic: Word overlap and TF-IDF. Crude, cheap, and they work. This is the bar every unit has to clear.

landmarks.gave: The neutral null: most change is drift, so selection must beat that baseline.
landmarks.memetic: Already exists for culture (random copying of baby names and pottery). It must be fitted before any selection claim. The one selection test here had 27% power.
landmarks.statusText: theory exists; not yet applied here

landmarks.gave: One universal marker gave one tree of life.
landmarks.memetic: This is premise P2: a set of units present in every model and robust to wording. Only 1 to 5% of neurons recur across retrained models.
landmarks.statusText: the hope behind P2; weak so far

landmarks.gave: Cheap, accurate reading with a known error rate.
landmarks.memetic: The most natural role for neuron reading. Not yet earned: the reader mostly reads words and has no stated error rate against ground truth.
landmarks.statusText: this is where memetics is now

landmarks.memetic: For models, catalogues of neuron descriptions exist. A reference list of validated meme units for one public model is cheap to build. A parts list is not function.

landmarks.gave: A cell stripped to the genes it cannot live without, some with unknown function.
landmarks.memetic: A model run on the strongest 8% of its neuron activations per token loses little: loss rises 2.9%. It still depends on a band of weaker activity whose function is unclear. Whether the dense 8B models used here are sparse in the same way is untested.
